input.body:
## `Claudinite executor` regression (29s → 53s): investigated, not a code slowdown — closing with no fix

Followed the `ci-performance-evaluation` skill. Summary: the step breakdown and per-item cost are
unchanged between the two windows; the median moved because the **previous window's runs happened
to batch far fewer items each**, not because any item got slower to process.

### 1. Step breakdown

Across every sampled run, `Set up job` + `checkout` + `setup-node` together cost 2-8s and are flat.
100% of the variance is in **`Pick up and execute ready work`**, which runs
`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs` (vendored engine code, not owned by
this repo).

### 2. The dominant cost is per-item, not fixed

Every item the executor touches — whether it ends in a `code_work`-only outcome (`task-janitor`,
`usage-fold`, `logs-prune`, `claudinite-lifecycle/update`) or an agent handoff — pays a **~15-20s
GitHub API round trip** (the "target — no open PR to amend/supersede" check plus the label/comment
writes) on top of whatever the item's own work costs (often just 1-7s). That per-item cost is
**identical in both windows**:

- This window, single-item runs: `#403 logs-prune` — 23s total (16.5s target-check + 3.3s work + 2.9s
  final check). `#385 logs-prune` — 21s total, same shape.
- Previous window, a 9-item run (`33303773837`, 2026-08-30T09:19): `#299` lifecycle-update, `#291`
  ci-performance, `#292` growth-dedup, `#293` growth-discover-packs, `#295` rule-revalidation, `#294`
  prose-to-checks-sweep, `#297` task-janitor, `#296` lifecycle-update, `#298` tidy-prs — 97s total,
  ~10-15s/item, same target-check-dominated shape.

No item type got measurably slower. There's nothing in the profile pointing at a code regression in
the vendored executor.

### 3. What actually moved: items processed per run

| | this window (n=11) | previous window (n=17) |
|---|---|---|
| step-4 median | ~55s | ~24s |
| items/run (sampled) | 1, 1, 3, 3, 4, ... | mostly 0-1, with occasional bursts up to 9 |
| dispatch cadence | ~2x/day, matching the scheduler's fixed cron anchors | up to 7 `workflow_dispatch` runs in a single day (13-90 min apart) |

The scheduler (`claudinite-scheduler.yml`) fires on a fixed twice-daily cron. This window's executor
runs land right on those two anchors and each processes whatever accumulated since the last one (1-4
items, mostly ready-made standing tasks). The previous window shows a much higher rate of
`workflow_dispatch` executor runs clustered together (matching the burst of
"Claudinite update: N packs upgraded" commits from that period's active pack rollout) — those runs
kept draining the queue every 15-90 minutes, so most of them picked up 0-1 items, which pulls the
window's median step-4 duration down. It's an artifact of comparing a high-frequency dispatch period
against the steady-state cadence, not a change in the steady-state itself.

### 4. Conclusion — no fix, no PR

Per-item cost is flat and is inherent to the design (a GitHub API round trip per item); there's no
evidence of an actual slowdown to chase, and the fix for "runs take longer when more items queue up
between fixed cron anchors" would be to fire the scheduler more often — a cadence change, not a
performance bug, and outside this task's scope. Leaving the executor and scheduler as they are.

Method: the `ci-performance-evaluation` skill, steps 1-2 (further steps weren't reached because
step 1/2 already explained the delta without pointing at a real regression).

entries.name: mcp__github__issue_write
entries.description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

delete.description: Set to true to clear this field's current value on the issue. When false or omitted, this property is ignored. Cannot be true when 'value' or 'field_option_name' is provided.

field_name.description: Issue field name (case-insensitive). Must match a field returned by list_issue_fields for this repository or its organization.

field_option_name.description: Option name for single-select fields. Validated against the field's options before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'value' or 'delete: true'.

value.description: Value to set. Use for text, number, and date fields (date as YYYY-MM-DD). For single-select fields, prefer 'field_option_name' so the option is validated before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'field_option_name' or 'delete: true'.

issue_fields.description: Issue field values to set or clear. Each item requires 'field_name' and exactly one of 'value', 'field_option_name', or 'delete: true'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
- 'create' - creates a new issue.
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

parent_issue_number.description: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

parent_owner.description: Repository owner of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_repo. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

parent_repo.description: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. For updates, pass null to remove the current type. Only use if issue types are enabled for this repository. Use list_issue_types to get valid type values for this repository or its owner organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.
